test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 30 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A piece of cake

options.text: A slice of cake for eating
A cake which is sold as a piece
A cake that broke into pieces

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. Easy to do or achieve.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"A piece of cake"** means something that is very easy to do or achieve. (बहुत आसान काम)

 
 
• **English Meaning:** It refers to a task or activity that requires little to no effort.
 
• **Hindi Meaning:** यह एक ऐसा कार्य है जो करने में बहुत आसान होता है।
 
 
 
• **Example:** Solving that math problem was a piece of cake for her.
 
• **Explanation:** The idiom does not literally refer to cake, but it metaphorically implies simplicity or ease in accomplishing something.
 
• **Hindi Meaning:** यह मुहावरा सचमुच के केक के बारे में नहीं है, बल्कि यह किसी काम को सरलता से पूरा करने का संकेत देता है।
 
• **Example:** Baking cookies is a piece of cake for my mom.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. Easy to do or achieve.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings:

__
 
• **Option 1: A slice of cake for eating** (खाने के लिए केक का एक टुकड़ा): This refers to a literal slice of cake, which is unrelated to the idiom.

 
 
• **Example:** She served me a delicious slice of cake at the party.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: A cake which is sold as a piece** (एक केक जो टुकड़ों में बेचा जाता है): This refers to cake being sold in portions, which is not the meaning of the idiom.
 
 
• **Example:** The bakery sells cakes in individual pieces.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: A cake that broke into pieces** (एक केक जो टुकड़ों में टूट गया है): This refers to a physical cake that has crumbled, which is unrelated to the idiom.
 
 
• **Example:** The cake fell on the floor and broke into pieces.
